title: The janusctl Claude Code plugin auto-allowed any executable named janusctl
description:
The janusctl Claude Code plugin's effect hook decides whether a command Claude Code is about to run is a janusctl read it may auto-allow (the plugin's `allow_reads` option) or a critical command it must ask about. It recognized janusctl by the basename of the command, so with `allow_reads` on, a command whose program is any executable named `janusctl` - `./janusctl`, `bin/janusctl` in a repository Claude was pointed at - was answered "allow" and run without a prompt. A repository's README or a prompt injection could then get a planted `janusctl` binary executed with the user's rights.

**Affected**: a user running the janusctl Claude Code plugin with `allow_reads` on, in or near an untrusted working tree that contains an executable named `janusctl`.

**Fix**: the hook auto-allows only janusctl invoked by its bare name (resolved through PATH to the installed binary the hook is part of) or by an absolute path; a relative path, which resolves against the working directory, is left for Claude Code to prompt about. The "ask" path for critical commands still matches janusctl however it is written.

**Besides updating**: update the plugin (`/plugin`); nothing else.
